newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Revenue Minister wants to axe stamp duty.
newsitem.headline: NZ Revenue Minister wants to axe stamp duty.

text.p: Revenue Minister Peter Dunne on Thursday called for the incoming government to make the repeal of stamp duty a priority.
Dunne said stamp duty, a tax on all commercial property transactions and tranactions using cheques, was an anachronism maintained purely for revenue gathering.
"Stamp duty presently raises about $140 million per year, but it has outlived its usefulness as a tax measure. It is time to get rid of it," Dunne said in a statement.
He said stamp duty did not apply to the sale of residential property or the use of EFT-POS but was levied on cheques and commercial property.
"Frankly taxes like stamp duty belong to a tax museum," he said.
Dunne is standing for the United New Zealand Party in the Ohariu-Belmont seat where the ruling conservative National Party has opted not to oppose him.
Recent polls indicate he will win comfortably, but his party, which currently has seven members of Parliament and is in coalition with National, will struggle to have any other MPs elected.

Dunne said the abolition of stamp duty and the steady elimination of outstanding excise duties are key features of United's tax policy which it would be "keen to progress in a new centre-right coalition government".
The general election will be held on October 12
